title: Residency & Retention Automaudit Orchestrator: drift detection, remediation, and evidence packaging
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build an orchestration service (Automaudit Orchestrator) that continuously evaluates data residency and retention configurations across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments, detects configuration drift from the canonical policy-as-code source, performs safe automated remediation where allowed, and generates tamper-evident evidence bundles for auditors.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator reads canonical residency & retention policies from the policy-as-code repo and canonicalizes incoming config from Console, Dedicated control plane, and Private agents
Drift detector calculates a drift score and a human-readable diff for each tenant / deployment; drift events persist to Audit Store and raise alerts when score >= threshold
Autoremediate path executes safe remediation steps for low-risk mismatches (e.g., retention longer than allowed) with canary/dry-run modes and operator approval workflows for high-risk changes
Evidence packaging produces signed, encrypted bundles (policy snapshot, detected diffs, remediation steps, timestamps) stored in S3/GCS and referenced in the Linear ticket and audit log
End-to-end tests validate detection, remediation, and evidence generation in a staging environment; no regressions introduced to existing residency guardrails
technical_design: Architecture: controller + fleet agents. Controller reads policy-as-code (Terraform/JSON schema) and reconciles against inventory of config sources via adapters (Console API, Dedicated Control Plane API, Private Agent RPC)
Detection: schema-aware comparator with weighting for residency vs retention vs encryption/KMS settings; computes drift_score (0-100) and human diff; flags where enforcement_mode != 'enforced'
Remediation: two modes - automatic (allowlisted tenants, low-risk diffs) and suggested (creates remediation PR + rollback plan). All remediation actions are idempotent and state-checked before/after
Evidence: ephemeral evidence bundle signed with platform KMS key and encrypted with customer KMS when available; store reference in Audit Store and emit webhook to compliance webhook endpoint

Observability: per-tenant metrics (drift_rate, time_to_remediate), tracing headers for each reconciliation, audit events shipped to Splunk/Datadog. Alerts via PagerDuty + Slack channel #compliance-alerts
Security: operator approval flow enforces RBAC; remediation service runs with least privilege; security_review_required = true for the release
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Dry run: run detection against staging environment for 2 weeks, no remediation, collect false-positive metrics
Phase 1 - Canary remediation: enable automatic remediation for 5 internal tenants with operator approvals logged; monitor for 72h
Phase 2 - Tiered rollout: enable auto remediation for customers on Dedicated that opted in; customers can opt-out via Console toggle
Phase 3 - Enforcement: enable full enforcement for high-risk policy violations for new Dedicated and Private deployments release-locked to private-2.4
Rollback: immediate disable toggle at controller level + automated reconciliation to previous state; documented runbook in Confluence
test_plan: Unit tests for comparator logic and drift scoring (>= 95% coverage)
Integration tests: simulate drift from Console/Dedicated/Private Agent and validate detection, remediation, and evidence storage
Chaos: introduce transient API failures to ensure reconciliation is idempotent and retriable
Security tests: KMS signing/verification of evidence bundles and RBAC path tests
E2E: staged canary run in staging with audit evidence verified by Compliance team
